name: Shangani
tagline: The tourist-friendly waterfront edge of the old town
description: Shangani sits on Stone Town's western tip, home to boutique hotels, rooftop restaurants, and the best sunset views over the harbor. It is the most polished and walkable part of the old town, with the highest concentration of laptop-tolerant cafes and reliable-ish wifi, though still patchy by global standards.
bestFor: short stays, first-time visitors, sunset views
pros: Most laptop-friendly cafes in the old town
Easy walk to Forodhani Gardens night market
cons: Most expensive part of Stone Town

name: Mkunazini
tagline: The historic heart, near the old slave market and cathedral
description: Mkunazini is central Stone Town, dense with coral-stone houses, the Anglican Cathedral built on the site of the old slave market, and quiet residential alleys just steps from the busier tourist routes. It offers a more local, lived-in feel with cheaper guesthouses, though wifi and power reliability are weaker here than in Shangani.
bestFor: budget guesthouse stays, history and culture focus
cons: Weaker wifi and more frequent power cuts
Easy to get disoriented in the alley maze at night

name: Forodhani / Malindi waterfront
tagline: The night-market and port district on the northern shorefront
description: This stretch runs from Forodhani Gardens, famous for its evening street-food market, up to the Malindi area near the old dhow harbor and ferry port. It is lively at night with grilled seafood stalls and local families, and practical by day for ferry connections to Dar es Salaam, though it can feel congested and less private.
bestFor: food lovers, short layovers before ferry connections
pros: Best street food in Stone Town at Forodhani market
Walking distance to the ferry port for Dar es Salaam
Constant social energy in the evenings
cons: Crowded and noisy near the port by day
Higher petty-theft risk in the market crowds

name: Paje
tagline: The east-coast kitesurf and coworking beach town
description: About 45-60 minutes from Stone Town by road, Paje is where most Zanzibar-based nomads actually settle long-term, drawn by kitesurfing, real coworking spaces, beach bars, and a denser expat community than the old town offers. It trades cultural depth for reliable infrastructure and an active, social beach-town lifestyle.
pros: Actual coworking spaces and better wifi
Strong long-term nomad and kitesurf community
Beautiful beach right outside your door
cons: 45-60 minute drive from Stone Town's culture and ferry port
Can feel like a bubble, less authentically Zanzibari
